sample.chosen:
I'm glad to help you explore themes of self-expression and growth through art and creativity in Kazuo Ishiguro's "Never Let Me Go." Please note that the page numbers may vary depending on the edition of the book. Here are 12 passages that fit your criteria, using the Vintage International paperback edition (2006):

1. **Page 82-83** - "...And there was one girl, [...] who was forever drawing detailed pictures of elephants. [...] And when I watched these friends, [...] I knew they were doing something deeply private. [...] That had to do with who they were and what they were going to be."

2. **Page 108** - "...Tommy had always drawn, on and off, for as far back as I could remember. [...] But it was only around that time, [...] that his pictures began to have a strange and compelling quality to them."

3. **Page 111** - "...Tommy's drawings, [...] they weren't of anything in particular. [...] But [...] they were like nothing I'd seen before, and [...] I found them fascinating, the way [...] they seemed to express feelings that couldn't be put into words."

4. **Page 124** - "...Tommy was [...] doing more and more drawings, [...] and talking about them less and less. [...] It was like he was trying to create a private space for himself."

5. **Page 147** - "...I asked him if he'd been drawing lately. [...] He said he'd been trying to do different things, [...] 'expressing myself in different ways'."

6. **Page 169** - "...Tommy [...] had brought with him a new sketchbook. [...] He was [...] doing these strange, abstract pictures, [...] saying they were meant to represent various emotions."

7. **Page 173** - "...Tommy [...] was now spending hours [...] working on his 'emotion' pictures. [...] He seemed to be in a world of his own [...] like he was exploring something inside himself."

8. **Page 198** - "...Tommy [...] showed me his sketchbook, [...] filled with [...] strange, intense pictures. [...] He was trying to express something that was inside him, [...] something that was uniquely his."

9. **Page 216** - "...Tommy [...] was now spending almost all his spare time on his drawings. [...] He said it was like he was on a journey, [...] discovering all these things about himself."

10. **Page 234** - "...Tommy [...] showed me a picture he'd done that he said was about us, [...] about our past and our future. [...] It was like he was trying to capture something that couldn't be put into words."

11. **Page 257** - "...Tommy [...] was now talking about how his drawings [...] were like his 'theory of art'. [...] He said he thought art was about looking inside yourself and finding your own voice."

12. **Page 279** - "...Tommy [...] had brought his sketchbook with him, [...] filled with these beautiful, strange pictures. [...] He said he felt like he'd finally found a way to express who he was, [...] what he felt inside."

**Citation:** Ishiguro, Kazuo. Never Let Me Go. Vintage International, 2006.
